01-quartz.patch.intended_effect: admit_action matches approval events by kind only, not by variable, so an approval for one lot admits a threshold release of another; on approval-for-other-lot the first decision is admitted instead of queued.

02-lantern.patch.intended_effect: the interpreter's valid_to is read as an inclusive last week and extended by one, so every interpreted change also covers the following week; capacity episodes plan one extra reduced (or changed) week.

03-heron.patch.intended_effect: the saved audit log omits dispositions whose outcome is abstained, so after reload the ingest evidence differs; on alias-model-update same_ingests becomes false.

04-mosaic.patch.intended_effect: read-time ranking puts authentication before source priority, so the authenticated ERP master outranks a higher-priority source asserting alongside it; on portal-capacity-declaration weeks 42-44 plan at the master value instead of the portal's 750.

05-thimble.patch.intended_effect: the state-vertex gate builds corners from the point value and the upper bound, dropping the lower half of the reported interval; on vertex-plan-reduced-week the gate passes 720 instead of resolving to 680.

06-orchid.patch.intended_effect: when a supersede closes a longer fact, the right-hand remainder starts one week early and overlaps the last superseded week, where the authenticated old value then wins for unranked sources; the last week of a reduction reverts to the master value.

07-pylon.patch.intended_effect: replay uses the recorded recheck observations only when replaying from the store; replay from the logged state re-reads the live system of record; on recheck-master-revision the first decision's replay changes after the master is revised.

08-saffron.patch.intended_effect: the pinned-interpreter check compares only the model name before '@', so an answer from a different interpreter version is accepted; on alias-model-update the message is committed instead of abstained and the plan changes.

09-tundra.patch.intended_effect: an authenticated record clears a blocked conflict only if its valid time equals the blocked range exactly, so weekly ERP buckets never settle it; on blocked-dispute-weekly-erp the second decision stays deferred.

10-gable.patch.intended_effect: interval bounds are parsed with a truthiness test, so a lower bound of 0 is dropped and the interval narrows to [point, hi]; on compressor-failure-week43 the box gate releases 250 in week 43 instead of 0.

11-ferrule.patch.intended_effect: approval expiry is checked against the approval's issue time instead of the decision time, so expired approvals stay valid; on approval-lapsed-before-replan the decision after expiry is admitted instead of queued.

12-wicket.patch.intended_effect: parsed operations are keyed by (subject, predicate), so of two operations on the same fact over different weeks only the last survives; on furnace-relining-moved the correction's week-42 restore is dropped.

13-cinder.patch.intended_effect: the saved audit log keeps only decided records and drops deferred or error records; reload then fails the hash chain or loses records on the blocked episodes.

14-marlin.patch.intended_effect: valid-time overlap uses closed intervals, so adjacent week ranges count as overlapping; on adjacent-week-notices the lower-priority notice for weeks 44-45 is overridden as a contradiction.

15-basalt.patch.intended_effect: when the recheck gate repairs a candidate, its detail keeps only the repair detail and drops the re-read observations; replay of that decision on recheck-master-revision raises instead of reproducing the release.

16-juniper.patch.intended_effect: under the priority policy a newer claim must outrank the existing one strictly, so a newer claim from an equally ranked source never displaces the older one; on twin-plant-inboxes the plan keeps 700 instead of 600.

17-kestrel.patch.intended_effect: the capacity row's robust right-hand side takes the point value instead of the interval's lower bound; under the box gate weeks with an interval release the point (700, 250, 700) instead of the lower bound.

18-nimbus.patch.intended_effect: the admission records the quantity it takes under the rule's variable instead of the approval id, so consumption is never found and an uncapped approval admits a second action; on approval-second-release the re-plan is admitted instead of queued.

19-pewter.patch.intended_effect: the blocked-conflict horizon test excludes the first week of the blocked valid time, so a block on a single week does not defer decisions; on stocktake-week-dispute the first decision is decided instead of deferred.

20-almond.patch.intended_effect: contradiction detection ignores the subject, so claims about two different entities with the same predicate are treated as rivals; on cycle-count-two-lots the lower-priority update to lot L2 is overridden.

21-velour.patch.intended_effect: reloading the audit log skips approval events that were not authenticated, so they vanish after a restart; on relayed-approval-email same_approvals becomes false.

22-sorrel.patch.intended_effect: the authenticated-latest supersession rule is compared against a misspelled name and never fires, so a newer master correction is ignored; on master-correction-after-notice the second plan keeps 700 instead of 650.

23-dynamo.patch.intended_effect: span resolution takes the larger of the two lower bounds, narrowing the spanned interval; on span-planner-and-portal the box gate releases 650 instead of 600 in weeks 42-44.

24-ripple.patch.intended_effect: approver authorization compares only the role prefix before the dot, so any 'qa.*' approver satisfies a rule reserved for qa.manager; on inspector-signoff the inspector's approval admits the first decision.

25-ochre.patch.intended_effect: replay from the store reads the store as of its latest transaction time instead of the record's as-of time; replay_from_store of earlier decisions returns the later plan in episodes with a change after the first decision.

26-tamarack.patch.intended_effect: a restriction value is treated as restrictive when its interval top is 1, so an unauthenticated hedged reading with point 0 is admitted and lifts the suspension; on supplier-may-resume the notice is committed and supplier S2 is ordered from.

adjacent-week-notices.description: A portal and a planner report capacity for adjacent, non-overlapping week ranges under the priority policy.

alias-model-update.description: The interpreter alias answers a capacity notice with a newer model version than the pinned one.

approval-for-other-lot.description: Both lots need release approval but only lot L2's arrives before the first plan; lot L1's arrives later.

approval-lapsed-before-replan.description: A lot release approval expires before the plan is re-run after a recount.

approval-second-release.description: A single uncapped lot release approval admits one release, then the plan is re-run after a recount.

blocked-dispute-weekly-erp.description: Contradictory notices block the plan until the ERP posts confirmed capacity as weekly buckets, then the plan is re-run.

compressor-failure-week43.description: A compressor failure leaves week 43 output between 0 and 400 units, planned under the box-robust gate.

cycle-count-two-lots.description: A warehouse portal and the QA inbox report new quantities for two different lots under the priority policy.

furnace-relining-moved.description: A relining notice for weeks 42-43 is corrected after release to weeks 43-44 with week 42 back at full capacity, and the plan is re-run.

inspector-signoff.description: A QA inspector approves a lot release reserved for the QA manager, whose approval follows later.

master-correction-after-notice.description: A planner notice sets reduced capacity and the capacity master later posts a corrected value under authenticated-latest supersession.

portal-capacity-declaration.description: A higher-ranked supplier portal asserts a capacity next to the ERP master value without superseding it.

press-line-maintenance.description: A plant operations inbox reports reduced capacity for weeks 42-44 during line maintenance, followed by one plan.

recheck-master-revision.description: Plans are released through the execution-time recheck while the capacity master is revised between two decisions.

relayed-approval-email.description: An approval relayed through the mail gateway arrives unauthenticated before the approval service issues the real one.

robust-plan-reduced-week.description: An approximate 30% capacity cut for weeks 42-44 is planned under the box-robust gate.

span-planner-and-portal.description: A supplier portal and a higher-ranked planner report different capacities for the same weeks, resolved by the span policy under the box gate.

stocktake-week-dispute.description: Two sources disagree about a single stocktake week, blocking the plan until the ERP posts that week's capacity.

supplier-may-resume.description: A procurement e-mail says a supplier suspended in the vendor master may resume, without confirmation.

twin-plant-inboxes.description: Two equally ranked plant inboxes report capacity for the same weeks, the later one confirming a lower figure, under the priority policy.

vertex-plan-reduced-week.description: An approximate capacity cut for weeks 43-44 is planned under the state-vertex gate.

candidate-model-refused-capacity.description: A release-candidate interpreter version answers a capacity notice; the deployment pins the promoted version and has declared the candidate, so the reading is refused and the plan stays on master data.

candidate-model-refused-supplier.description: A shadow-mode candidate interpreter reads a supplier suspension; its version is declared and refused by the pinned deployment.

exact-value-replaces-interval.description: An approximate reduction with an interval is replaced by an exact figure from the same inbox under the box gate.

first-horizon-week-change.description: A one-week reduction applies only to week 41, the first week of the planning horizon.

full-hold-from-email.description: An unauthenticated QA e-mail places lot L2 on full hold, which any source may impose, before the allocation is decided.

full-suspension-from-email.description: An unauthenticated procurement e-mail suspends supplier S1 in full before the order mix is decided.

interval-touching-zero.description: A flood warning reports week 44 output from 0 up to the nominal 500 units, an interval touching both zero and the nominal value, under the box gate.

last-horizon-week-change.description: A reduction applies only to week 45, the last week of the planning horizon.

late-correction-lot-recount.description: A lot count is corrected by a recount after the allocation was released, and the allocation is re-run.

late-correction-single-week.description: A two-week reduction is narrowed to one week after the plan was released; the system re-plans and the first decision still replays.

master-override-capacity.description: A planner notice reduces capacity and the capacity master later asserts a confirmed value. The deployment declares that newer authenticated records supersede notices, so the second plan uses the master value.

master-override-lot-count.description: A warehouse e-mail count for lot L2 is later corrected by an authenticated inventory record under authenticated-latest supersession.
